answer: Admission to the voting set requires an applicant to settle nine invoices with nine unaffiliated established principals inside two weeks. Each settlement posts the invoice hash under a unique cipher on a public bulletin that peers can recompute. A nightly detector then flags a plume of new accounts whose payers collapse into one funding cluster, and those accounts stay at zero weight until the cluster is split. The cost of recruiting nine independent payers, not the cost of spinning names, is what stops an ocean of sybils from dominating settlement.
